bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free standalone balance sheet: the Company states the Debt-Equity Ratio as on 31 March 2026 is Nil (previous year: Nil), the Company having no borrowings, and Interest Coverage Ratio is Not Applicable for the same reason
- Asset-light standalone investment operation with no trade receivables or inventory, so Debtors Turnover and Inventory Turnover Ratios are stated as Not Applicable
- Diversification of the securities-investment activity by an operating tea manufacturing business held through a wholly owned subsidiary
- Formalised risk-management and internal-control framework: internal audit per an Audit-Committee-approved annual plan, with Statutory Auditors confirming internal financial controls over financial reporting are adequate and operating effectively
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Investment value / investee performance risk — The Company states it is mainly exposed to market risks in the form of reduction in value of its investments and a fall in return due to a dip in the investee company's performance - the dominant exposure for a single-segment investment company.
- Borrower repayment delay and liquidity risk — Delay in repayment by the borrower companies can affect liquidity and redeployment scope, per the MD&A Risks and Concerns section.
- Economic and industry cycle exposure — The Company states it is exposed to fluctuation of economy and industry cycle; growth momentum is described as largely dependent on ongoing global events that pose downside risk.
- Business concentration in a single segment — The Company operates in a single segment - to invest, deal etc. in securities - with income concentrated in dividends, interest on loans, rental income, fixed deposits and profit on sale of investments, leaving no operating diversification at the standalone level.
- Competitive intensity from market volatility and inflation — High volatility in the market along with higher inflation has intensified the competition, per the Opportunities and Threats section.
- Climate and weather risk in the tea business — Climate change reduces both tea yield and quality, and changes in weather patterns affect the timing of the tea flushes, making production less predictable; changing climate patterns interfere with plucking, pruning and applying chemical inputs. Yield depends on weather, irrigation facilities and soil management as the area under plantation is constant.
- Tea input-cost inflation, labour shortage and import competition — Main challenges for the Indian tea industry include rising cost of wages, fertilizers, chemicals, power and fuel, transportation and packaging, labour shortages and import competition; input cost movements in tea and coffee continue to influence sector margins and pricing actions.
- Geopolitical disruption to macro conditions and supply — RBI has projected GDP growth to moderate to approximately 6.6% in FY 2026-27 reflecting downside risks from the geopolitical situation in the Middle East and the possibility of a below-normal monsoon; disruptions in availability of fuel or packaging material due to geopolitical events are being monitored, having been managed so far without affecting manufacturing and supply operations.

business.body: The Company operates in a single segment, which is to invest and deal in securities, earning income in the form of dividends, interest on loans, rental income, income from fixed deposits and profit on sale of investments. Apart from its securities-investment operations, it continues to be engaged in the business of tea manufacturing and processing through its subsidiary Cinnatolliah Tea Limited (CTL), whose main business is the manufacture and sale of tea. As per a letter dated 19 January 2024 from the Reserve Bank of India, the Company is an unregistered Core Investment Company (CIC); there was no change in the nature of business during the year.

outlook.body:
- Continue as a single-segment unregistered Core Investment Company investing and dealing in securities, earning dividends, interest on loans, rental income, fixed-deposit income and profit on sale of investments, with no change in the nature of business
- Retain tea manufacturing and processing exposure through the subsidiary Cinnatolliah Tea Limited alongside the securities-investment activity
- Strengthen core categories, scale growth platforms and build channels of the future, supported by brand investments and execution excellence
- Monitor geopolitical events affecting fuel and packaging availability and build resilience across the value chain to mitigate such disruptions
- At CTL, continue soil conservation measures and scientifically designed application of fertilizers and plant protection formulations to minimise environmental impact
- Operate a risk-management process for identification, categorisation and prioritisation of operational, financial, legal and other business risks, reviewed by the CFO with the Internal Auditor and reported to the Audit Committee
- Strengthen operative staff as and when the need arises, and attract talent from reputed institutions, with emphasis on a performance-oriented culture and the performance management system
- CTL has taken up adequate soil conservation measures, and application of chemical based inputs like fertilizers and plant protection formulations is carefully and scientifically designed to minimize the impact on the environment.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body:
- India capital market outlook remains positive, supported by strong economic fundamentals, favourable demographic trends and continued regulatory reforms; the market generated revenue of USD 3.8 Billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 6.8 Billion by 2034, a CAGR of 6.27% from 2026-2034
- Indian NBFC sector is expected to grow at a CAGR of 18.5% between 2021 and 2026 (per a ResearchAndMarkets.com report), driven by increasing demand for credit, government financial-inclusion initiatives and the rise of digitalisation
- Capital market expansion driven by rising retail investor participation, digital transformation of financial services (mobile trading applications, electronic KYC) and strong domestic economic fundamentals
- RBI has projected India GDP growth to moderate to approximately 6.6% in FY 2026-27, reflecting downside risks from the geopolitical situation in the Middle East and the possibility of a below-normal monsoon
- Capital investment is expected to be the dominant growth driver for the Indian economy in the medium term, supported by an initial revival in the investment cycle
- Indian tea market is projected to reach revenue of approximately USD 20,459.8 million by 2033, at a CAGR of 6.8% over 2026-2033
- Tea crop period runs March to December and yield depends on weather; the area under plantation is constant, so yield depends largely on irrigation facilities and better soil management techniques
- Middle East - particularly UAE, Iraq, Iran and Turkey - remained the primary engine of India's tea-export growth and continues to account for a significant share of India's tea exports, with exporters selectively diversifying into China and North Africa
- Input cost movements in agricultural commodities such as tea and coffee continue to influence sector margins and pricing actions
- Expected continued growth in health and wellness, functional teas, sustainability and experiential tea journeys as consumers become more informed and adventurous
- Indian equity market seen in an optimism zone on ebbing fear of rate hikes and a lower valuation premium for emerging markets, with India expected to remain a bright spot among emerging countries
